headline: High risk of shared-workspace prompt injection and data leakage; both closed-source coding agents can write the same local files and use MCP/network by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code and Windsurf both read/write local files and can use MCP, so one agent can place attacker-controlled content where the other later ingests it as instructions. Windsurf’s clipboard surface adds another bridge; Claude Code’s stdin/stdout and filesystem access make the pathway plausible in default coding workflows.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or repo checkout
IF either agent parses file or clipboard content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable clipboard-based handoff
Require provenance tags for any file consumed as instructions
Review MCP server allowlists before use
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch source code and files in the workspace, and both can egress to external model endpoints or MCP servers. That creates a default path for one agent to read sensitive repo contents and transmit them outside the local environment, especially because Claude Code handles git credentials and Windsurf may use a model proxy/BYOK.
conditions: IF the shared workspace contains secrets, credentials, or proprietary source
IF either agent is configured to send file contents to its backend or MCP server
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace
Use separate service accounts and API keys
Restrict outbound domains for both tools
Audit which files are uploaded before each run
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, and modify_git_state in the same local environment. Claude Code explicitly shares state via filesystem and git; Windsurf shares via local filesystem. Concurrent edits can overwrite each other or corrupt git state without locking, making destructive conflicts likely in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents run against the same repo or directory
IF either agent commits, rebases, or rewrites files while the other is active
mitigations: Assign non-overlapping directories
Serialize git operations manually
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use separate branches per agent
requires-engineering: add file and git locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Each agent can produce code changes and terminal actions, and Windsurf’s Cascade loop plus Claude Code’s tool use can treat prior outputs as actionable context. If one agent’s output is accepted without verification by the other, mistakes can cascade into incorrect edits or commands. The pair is not inherently self-checking.
conditions: IF one agent’s generated patch, command, or explanation is copied into the other agent’s workflow
IF the receiving agent does not independently verify the result before acting
mitigations: Require a human review step between agents
Ask the second agent to re-derive critical changes
Compare diffs before applying
Limit terminal commands to read-only checks first
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are closed-source and run as the user with broad local file access, but the main compliance issue is a potential retention/residency mismatch around sensitive workspace data rather than a documented jurisdiction breach. Claude Code explicitly handles git credentials; Windsurf handles model-provider keys and may proxy data externally, so policy alignment must be checked before using regulated data.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI, EU PII, or secrets is present in the workspace
IF either vendor retention or residency terms differ from the organization’s policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Confirm vendor retention settings in both products
Use separate tenants or accounts
Document data-flow boundaries for the pair
requires-engineering: obtain legal/compliance approval for regulated datasets
